pairs.distinction: Sleep is about nights; Tired is about days, including people who sleep fine but are drained by illness, work or caregiving.
pairs.reason: Plenty of people are exhausted without a sleep problem, and the sharper Tired line above makes that choice obvious.

pairs.distinction: Pain is hurting most days, whatever the cause; Illness is a condition that limits you, often without pain.
pairs.reason: Daily pain is common enough and specific enough that people look for it by name, and many limiting conditions don't hurt.

pairs.distinction: Illness is living with a condition; Healthcare is not being able to see a doctor when you need one.
pairs.reason: One is about your body and the other about the system around it, and many people have one without the other.

pairs.distinction: Hormones is losing days to a monthly cycle or menopause, which most people wouldn't call a condition.
pairs.reason: Someone losing days to periods or menopause wouldn't look under a heading about living with an illness.

pairs.distinction: Senses is losing sight or hearing over time; Disability is the world not being built for you.
pairs.reason: Many people losing their sight or hearing don't think of themselves as disabled, and many disabled people's problem is access, not their senses.

pairs.distinction: Teeth is dental care, which is insured and paid for separately from seeing a doctor.
pairs.reason: People who can see a doctor often still can't afford a dentist, and they name it on its own.

pairs.distinction: Diet is what you eat; Fitness is how fit and active you feel.
pairs.reason: Someone can eat well and still feel out of shape, or the reverse, so the choice is easy.

pairs.distinction: Tired is physical tiredness from any cause; Burnout is being used up by work.
pairs.reason: Burnout sits under Work and names the cause, while Tired is for anyone worn out whatever the reason.

pairs.distinction: Healthcare is not being able to see a doctor; Medical bills is worrying about what care will cost.
pairs.reason: Getting seen and paying for it are different worries, and the societal page already frames cost as a shared problem.

pairs.distinction: Diet is not eating the way you want; running out of food is not having enough to eat.
pairs.reason: Not having enough food is a money problem and belongs under Money, while Diet is about the kind of food you eat.

pairs.distinction: Disability is places and services not built for you; Discrimination is people treating you worse because of who you are.
pairs.reason: A missing ramp and being treated worse by a person are different problems, and one sits on each page.
